title: Chainalysis says hackers obtained credentials and live tokens for all of its users
tldr: Chainalysis, whose tools trace cryptocurrency flows, now says names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for every user were exposed, widening an incident first described as limited.

title: DigiCert says a 16-month exposure of an internal system let an outsider read customer identity documents
tldr: DigiCert says a server migration left an internal archive reachable from the internet from February 2025, and an unauthorized account read some customer records in June and July 2026.

title: Fox completes its $22 billion acquisition of Roku, five months after announcing it
tldr: Fox closed its $22 billion purchase of Roku, which reaches more than 100 million households, far earlier than the first-half-2027 completion the companies had projected.

title: AST SpaceMobile plans its own medium-lift rocket, backed by a $1.3 billion Firefly engine deal
tldr: The direct-to-phone satellite company says it will build Blacklift, a 20-ton-class rocket, and has committed $1.3 billion to Firefly for engines, a license and engineering support.

title: FaultScope: A software package for fast error attribution in quantum error correction
tldr: FaultScope is an open-source simulator that estimates how much each noisy component contributes to logical errors in quantum error correction, at under 1% extra runtime in tests.
byline: Yuguo Shao, Zhenyu Chen, Ningfeng Wang et al. · Yau Mathematical Sciences Center, Tsinghua University; Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications; Department of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University

title: OpenSSH patch fixes "*sshole", a ten-year-old login bypass on musl-based Linux systems
tldr: OpenSSH 10.6p2 fixes a flaw, present since 2016, that lets an oversized password log in to accounts meant to refuse passwords on musl-based Linux systems such as Alpine.

title: Blue Origin pushes the next New Glenn launch into January 2027 after May launchpad explosion
tldr: Blue Origin's CEO told staff the next New Glenn flight is now targeted for January 2027, after earlier hopes of launching before the end of this year.

title: FAA begins replacing floppy-disk-based air traffic displays with a digital system at more than 400 facilities
tldr: The FAA says it will replace 1980s display systems that run on floppy disks with the digital E-IDS platform, targeting 435 sites by the end of 2028.

title: Beyond Sensitive APIs: Detecting Access Control Flaws at Sensitive Callsites in Android Firmware
tldr: Callix, a tool that judges whether access checks are strong enough for a sensitive operation, found 819 vulnerable paths in pre-installed apps from ten Android vendors.
byline: Haotian Deng, Meng Hao, Hanxiao Chen et al. · University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

title: Second wave of attacks on refrigeration controllers hits supermarkets across Europe
tldr: Remote tampering with refrigeration controllers raised temperatures in more than 115 stores in six European countries on November 2, and also reached a French blood-service supplier, following a larger French wave in October.

title: Zyxel patches a switch flaw that was exploited on nearly 1,000 devices after being mistaken for an older bug
tldr: Zyxel fixed CVE-2026-107441 in ten GS1900 switch models after attackers used it to compromise 996 devices; the bug had been misattributed to an earlier, already-patched flaw.

title: Suspected Russian hackers use patched iPhone and Android flaws in watering-hole attacks
tldr: Sekoia says a group it links to Russia's foreign intelligence service used websites to profile visitors and attack phones that had not installed existing security updates.

title: DreamHost confirms a two-month breach of its File Manager exposed FTP logins and webmail sessions
tldr: Web host DreamHost says an attacker exploited a flaw in its File Manager from August to October 23, stealing FTP/SFTP credentials and some webmail session data.

title: Marvell agrees to buy Lumentum for $115 billion in an all-stock deal
tldr: Chip designer Marvell will acquire optical component maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion including debt, expected to close in the first half of 2028.

title: Google and partners dismantle XCPE botnet built into 1.3 million Android TV boxes
tldr: Google's Threat Intelligence Group and partners disrupted XCPE, a backdoor that a Chinese manufacturer shipped in more than 1.3 million Android TV boxes to rent out owners' internet connections.
byline: Krebs on Security, Ars Technica, The Register

title: Binance says a fake job interview started its $6.3 billion theft
tldr: Binance's incident report says a multi-stage attack beginning with a fake recruiter and malware led to the October 29 theft of about $6.34 billion, which the FBI attributed to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.

title: Apple warns memory costs are unprecedented as they squeeze margins and Mac supply
tldr: On its earnings call, Apple said memory pricing is unprecedented, forecast a December-quarter gross margin of 45 to 46 percent and expects Mac and iPad supply constraints.
